rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Refining turns extracted metal into usable metal. **Distillation** exploits volatility (zinc bp 907 °C, mercury); **liquation** exploits low melting point (tin flows off an inclined hearth at 232 °C leaving Fe and C behind); **poling** stirs molten crude copper with green wood whose hydrocarbons reduce dissolved Cu₂O and whose steam stirs and shields; and **electrolytic refinement** — the precision method —…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Anode: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ - Cathode: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu - Poling: 2Cu₂O + C → 4Cu + CO₂ (reduction by wood gases) - Zn bp 907 °C (distillation); Sn mp 232 °C (liquation)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: refining of metals, poling, electro-refinement (within Chemistry of Metals).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "In the electrolytic refining of copper the impure metal is the anode, pure copper is deposited on the cathode, and the noble metals collect as anode mud."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The mud that pays*** — a copper refinery processing 200,000 t of anodes a year recovers tonnes of silver and hundreds of kilograms of gold from anode mud; the "impurity" funds the purification.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Last 0.1 % Extraction gets the metal; **refining** makes it usable — copper must reach 99.99 % for wiring, otherwise its resistance and machinability collapse. This topic covers the purification toolkit: liquation, distillation, oxidation (poling), and the workhorse — **electrolytic refinement** (verified PYQ NEB 2024 on copper).  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Why crude metal is impure - Blast-furnace/reduction metal carries dissolved C, S, P, Si (from coke and flux), other reduced metals (Pb in Ag, Fe in Cu), and mechanically trapped slag. Each impurity dictates its own removal method. ### 2.2 Refining methods - **Distillation** — for volatile metals: Zn (bp 907 °C), Hg, Cd are distilled off from less volatile impurities.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Method by property: volatile -> distil (Zn/Hg); low mp -> liquate (Sn/Pb); oxide in melt -> pole (Cu); high purity -> electrolyse (Cu/Ag/Au). Anode mud = nobler than Cu; solution residues = baser.

Why must the poles be of green wood?** — **Poling** is a refining step for molten crude metal — chiefly copper — in which the melt is stirred with poles of green wood while it is covered with an inert material.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Electrorefining is electrode-potential sorting: copper is the only metal that both leaves the anode and accepts electrons at the cathode; everyone baser stays dissolved, everyone nobler stays solid — one tank, three-way separation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Crude metal carries C, S, P, Si, other metals, slag. Methods: distillation (volatile Zn 907 C, Hg, Cd), liquation (low-melting Sn 232 C, Pb on inclined hearth), poling (green wood poles reduce Cu2O in molten Cu; steam stirs + shields; hydrocarbons reduce), electrorefining (impure anode, pure cathode, acidified CuSO4).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Copper for electrical use must be 99.99 % pure: 0.05 % of arsenic raises its resistance enough to waste megawatts on a national grid — hence electrolytic copper, "Cu-ETP".

Common Confusions **Poling refines, it does not extract:** poling happens on molten metal already won; it removes dissolved oxide (Cu₂O), not ore.  ·  **Anode mud is not slag:** it is the *noblest* impurities — they are valuable (Ag, Au, Pt), not waste; their sale often pays the refining bill.

rows.text: **Baser impurities do not deposit:** Zn²⁺/Fe²⁺/Ni²⁺ from the anode remain in the electrolyte because Cu²⁺ reduces at a higher potential; the electrolyte is periodically bled and refreshed.  ·  ## 7.
